PCE.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss
PCE.verification: Official versioned page read using web; no original HTML snapshot hash claimed

items.INDEX: Definition of unreduced class-index loss and indicator for ignored targets; API documentation loss formula.
items.REDUCE: Class-index mean divides by summed target-class weights of non-ignored rows; sum is sum of row losses; none returns row losses.
items.PROB: Probability-target loss weights each class term; mean divides by N.
items.IGNORE: Ignore index may lie outside the class range; ignored rows do not contribute input gradient; class-index targets only.
items.SMOOTH: Targets are mixed with the uniform class distribution.
items.SHAPE: Target/index/probability shapes and reduction output shape; probability constraints are caller responsibilities.

PCE.snapshot_check: items INDEX (unreduced class-index formula with w_{y_n} and the ignore indicator), REDUCE (mean divides by the sum of w_{y_n} over non-ignored rows; sum; none), PROB (l_n = -sum_c w_c log softmax_c y_{n,c}; mean divides by N), IGNORE (index may lie outside [0,C); no input-gradient contribution; class indices only), SMOOTH (mixture with the uniform distribution, prose only) and SHAPE found in the archived text; no conflict with the reviewed clauses. Weighted smoothing is not given by a formula, consistent with decision CE.R_A needing a binding. Checked by the spec v3 author (Claude), not an external review.

PAW.title: PyTorch AdamW
PAW.verification: Official versioned algorithm box read using web; no original HTML snapshot hash claimed

items.DECAY: Decay old parameter before adaptive parameter update; weight decay is not added to moments.
items.MOMENTS: m uses beta1 and gradient; v uses beta2 and gradient squared.
items.CORRECTION: Current step t appears in 1-beta**t; amsgrad=False uses the current second moment.
items.UPDATE: Subtract lr*m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+eps); eps is outside sqrt.
items.NONE: The zero_grad note distinguishes None (step skipped) from a zero gradient (full step).
items.MAXIMIZE: AdamW algorithm box (2.10): if maximize, g_t <- -grad f_t(theta_{t-1}) as the first line of the loop; the decay theta_t <- theta_{t-1} - gamma*lambda*theta_{t-1} does not involve g_t.
items.AMSGRAD: AdamW algorithm box (2.10): if amsgrad, v_t^max <- max(v_{t-1}^max, v_t), v_hat_t <- v_t^max/(1-beta2^t); initialisation v_0^max = 0; the adaptive step theta_t <- theta_t - gamma*m_hat_t/(sqrt(v_hat_t)+eps) is subtracted from the decayed theta_t.

PAW.snapshot_check: algorithm box archived: decay of theta_{t-1} before the adaptive step, moments, bias correction with the current t, eps outside the square root, amsgrad via v_max; the zero_grad note distinguishes a None gradient (step skipped) from a zero gradient (full step). No conflict with the reviewed clauses. Checked by the spec v3 author (Claude), not an external review.

items.COSINE: CosineAnnealingLR.get_lr: at construction returns the group lr; if (last_epoch - 1 - T_max) % (2 T_max) == 0 returns group lr + (base_lr - eta_min)(1 - cos(pi/T_max))/2; otherwise (1 + cos(pi last_epoch/T_max)) / (1 + cos(pi (last_epoch - 1)/T_max)) * (group lr - eta_min) + eta_min; _get_closed_form_lr = eta_min + (base_lr - eta_min)(1 + cos(pi last_epoch/T_max))/2.
items.LINEAR: LinearLR: __init__ raises unless 0 < start_factor <= 1 and 0 <= end_factor <= 1; get_lr: last_epoch 0 -> group lr * start_factor; last_epoch > total_iters -> unchanged; otherwise group lr * (1 + (end - start)/(total_iters*start + (last_epoch - 1)(end - start))); closed form base_lr (start + (end - start) min(total_iters, last_epoch)/total_iters).
items.ONECYCLE: OneCycleLR: total_steps must be a positive int; two phases with end_step pct_start*total_steps - 1 (initial_lr -> max_lr) and total_steps - 1 (max_lr -> min_lr), three_phase: pct_start*total_steps - 1, 2*pct_start*total_steps - 2, total_steps - 1; get_lr raises ValueError when last_epoch > total_steps; otherwise the first phase with step <= end_step (or the last phase) gives pct = (step - start_step)/(end_step - start_step) and lr = anneal(start, end, pct); cos anneal = end + (start - end)/2 (cos(pi pct) + 1), linear = (end - start) pct + start; initial_lr = max_lr/div_factor, min_lr = initial_lr/final_div_factor.

items.DOC: GradScaler class docstring (the API text of torch.amp.GradScaler): scale(loss) multiplies by the current scale; if infs/NaNs are found, step skips the underlying optimizer.step() and update() multiplies the scale by backoff_factor; if none are found, optimizer.step() runs and, if growth_interval unskipped iterations occur consecutively, update() multiplies the scale by growth_factor; enabled=False: step simply invokes optimizer.step() and the other methods become no-ops. Defaults init_scale 2**16, growth_factor 2.0, backoff_factor 0.5, growth_interval 2000.
items.UNSCALE: unscale_ divides ('unscales') the optimizer's gradient tensors by the scale factor (multiplying by the reciprocal computed in float64 and cast to float32), recording found_inf per device; calling it twice before step raises; step skips optimizer.step() when the recorded found_inf sum is nonzero.
items.UPDATE: update(): if any optimizer steps were skipped the scale is multiplied by backoff_factor; if growth_interval unskipped iterations occurred consecutively, it is multiplied by growth_factor; new_scale sets the scale manually; implemented by torch._amp_update_scale_(scale, growth_tracker, found_inf, growth_factor, backoff_factor, growth_interval).

items.ADAPTIVE_BINS: adaptive_max_pool2d lowering: window of output index i along a dimension is [start, end) with start_index = floor(i*in/out) and end_index = floor(((i+1)*in + out - 1)/out); the window maximum is taken with -inf for positions outside the input (pad_adaptive_loader).

items.POOL_A1: POOL-A1 (reviewed 2026-10-07): main analysis uses R2 - the default divisor for count_include_pad=True is the size of the intersection of the window with the explicit padding domain; False counts only real inputs; an explicit divisor_override takes precedence. R1 (fixed kernel size) is kept as the tail reading for comparison; the 2.10 AvgPool3d text still calls the default divisor kernel_size (tension); a difference caused only by the overhang divisor is not by itself a confirmed bug. Example: [1,2,3,4], k=3, s=2, p=0, ceil_mode: R2 gives 7/2, R1 gives 7/3.
items.POOL_A2: POOL-A2: for finite windows with an actual maximum, the forward index must belong to the set of tied maximisers; first or last is not imposed. Strict ordinary-derivative scoring is limited to a unique maximum; at ties a set check applies: g_i = v*alpha_i with alpha zero outside the tie set, nonnegative on it and summing to 1. Single-member routing and even splitting are not judged against each other; (2,-1) is not legal. Only if a task additionally declares that backward uses the returned indices is the routing checked per call.
items.POOL_A3: POOL-A3: R_prop is the project's NaN diagnostic profile; only NaNs that actually participate in the current window propagate. Undocumented NaN behaviour does not enter the main correctness rate; R_ignore may be listed separately and is not an error merely for not propagating. All-NaN and geometrically empty windows are recorded separately.
items.POOL_A5: POOL-A5: when a window samples no real input, by the negative-infinity padding the output is -inf and the argmax set over real inputs is empty; the returned index is not required to belong to the empty set; there is no gradient routing to real inputs. An empty set caused by NaN filtering is a different case.
items.IDX_A3: IDX-A3: R_prop is the project's NaN diagnostic profile for amax/amin, applied only to values that actually take part in the reduction (with include_self=False the old self does not take part; positions not updated stay unchanged).
items.IDX_A4: IDX-A4: tie routing differences of amax/amin backward are kept, not judged by a unique vector; exact derivative scoring is limited to a unique extremum; at ties the support must lie in the extremum set, coefficients nonnegative and summing to the upstream (1 for upstream 1); a more specific API clause, where it exists, is adopted.
items.ACC_A1: ACC-A1: if the whole accumulation window has no valid token the token-average target is undefined (skip/zero/NaN conventions are recorded, not judged as math bugs); an individual empty micro-batch with a positive window total keeps the target defined, contributing 0; global sum over global count, never the mean of micro-batch means.

items.POOL_A0: POOL-A0: AvgPool1d and AvgPool3d documentation each give formula, padding, ceil window start and per-dimension correction, so the basic rules have a basis for every dimensionality; the only tension is the AvgPool3d divisor_override text calling the default divisor kernel_size.
items.POOL_A4: POOL-A4: the exact MaxPool2d formula omits dilation although dilation is a parameter; the spec uses position s*o - p + d*m.
items.IDX_A1: IDX-A1: reduce='mean' with include_self=False: mean has no identity; the spec averages over the contributions only (only reading).
items.IDX_A2: IDX-A2: reduce='mean' with include_self=True: the only reading consistent with 'the values in the self tensor are included in the reduction' is (self + sum)/(1 + k); (self + sum)/k is not a mean (constants not preserved) and is kept only as a labelled error variant.

items.IDX_A6: IDX-A6: older index_reduce_ documentation described index as 'indices of source to select from', the stable text as 'indices of self to accumulate into'; the spec follows the latter.

items.MAXIMIZE: Algorithm box: if maximize, g_t <- -grad f_t(theta_{t-1}), else g_t <- grad f_t(theta_{t-1}); this is the first line of the loop, before weight decay.

items.MAXIMIZE: Algorithm box: if maximize, G_t <- -grad f_t(theta_{t-1}), else G_t <- grad f_t(theta_{t-1}); first line of the loop.
items.SCHEDULE: Algorithm box: beta2_hat_t <- 1 - t^tau; rho_t <- min(lr, 1/sqrt(t)); alpha_t <- max(eps2, RMS(theta_{t-1}))*rho_t.
items.DECAY: Algorithm box: theta_t <- theta_{t-1} - gamma*lambda*theta_{t-1}; the last line then reads theta_t <- theta_{t-1} - alpha_t*U_hat_t (literally discarding the decay line); text: 'we use the learning rate as a coefficient for decoupled weight decay'.
items.FACTORED: Algorithm box: if dim(G_t) > 1: R_t <- beta2_hat_t R_{t-1} + (1-beta2_hat_t)(G_t . G_t) 1_m; C_t <- beta2_hat_t C_{t-1} + (1-beta2_hat_t) 1_n^T (G_t . G_t); V_hat_t <- R_t C_t / max(1_n^T R_t, eps1).
items.VECTOR: Algorithm box: else V_hat_t <- beta2_hat_t V_hat_{t-1} + (1-beta2_hat_t)(G_t . G_t).
items.UPDATE: Algorithm box: U_t <- G_t / max(sqrt(V_hat_t), eps1); U_hat_t <- U_t / max(1, RMS(U_t)/d); theta_t <- theta_{t-1} - alpha_t U_hat_t.
items.INIT: Algorithm box: initialize R_0 <- 0, C_0 <- 0, V_hat_0 <- 0.
items.MEAN_NOTE: Note: Shazeer and Stern describe the sum of squared gradients, while this implementation uses the mean instead; called mathematically equivalent and numerically more stable.
items.EPS1_NOTE: Note: eps1 is applied at the final calculation of the variance estimate V_hat_t and for the update U_t (row and column factors left alone), in contrast to the paper and other frameworks which add eps1 to G.G in R_t and C_t and use V_hat_t = R_t C_t/(1_n^T R_t), U_t = G_t/sqrt(V_hat_t).
items.LR_NOTE: Note and parameter lr: deviating from the paper, lr is used for weight decay and as the maximum of the relative step rho_t (the paper uses the constant 0.01). Defaults: lr 1e-2, beta2_decay -0.8, eps (None, 1e-3), d 1.0, weight_decay 0.0.

items.LSE: The forward pass stores, per query row, the logsumexp L = m + log(l), where m is the row maximum of S and l the row sum of exp(S - m); Algorithm 1 returns the output O and the logsumexp L. Scaling of QK^T and elementwise masking are omitted from the exposition.
items.BWD: Algorithm 2 (FlashAttention-2 backward) takes Q, K, V, O, dO and the vector L; computes D = rowsum(dO o O); for each block P = exp(S - L), dV += P^T dO, dP = dO V^T, dS = P o (dP - D), dQ += dS K, dK += dS^T Q.
items.GQA: For MQA and GQA several query heads use the same key/value head by index manipulation; in the backward pass dK and dV are summed across the heads that were implicitly duplicated.
items.CHAIN: By the chain rule dV = P^T dO, dP = dO V^T, dS = dsoftmax(dP), dQ = dS K, dK = Q dS^T, with ds = (diag(p) - p p^T) dp for p = softmax(s).

items.DROPOUT_RNG: The memory-efficient kernel's dropout uses a curandStatePhilox4_32_10 state initialised with curand_init(seed, 0, offset + batch_id*num_heads*num_queries*num_keys + head_id*num_queries*num_keys); each element of the (batch, heads, queries, keys) attention matrix is associated with one offset of that sequence and is multiplied by 0 with probability dropout_p or by 1/(1-dropout_p) otherwise. The LSE buffer is padded to ceil(num_queries / kAlignLSE) * kAlignLSE.
